_contract: LAM-ACCEPT WP-5 K-3. Applied by tools/lam/mission-dispatch.ps1 via --settings.
_authority: A worker implements one feature in one worktree and is visible only through artifacts, evidence and the agent view (design v2.3 SS9.3). It may write its worktree and its own evidence session; it may not touch the mission plane, publish, or edit the machinery that records it.
_plane_protection_is_guard_enforced: READ THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING THE MISSION PLANE IS UNPROTECTED HERE. K-3's restriction -- no .mission/** writes except exactly two closed members -- IS NOT WRITABLE AS PERMISSION RULES. Claude Code evaluates deny before allow, specificity does not change the order, and a deny rule cannot carry allowlist exceptions. This file used to carry Edit(.mission/**) in deny alongside both exceptions in allow, and the broad deny shadowed them: the number of exceptions that actually obtained was ZERO, not two. Measured by driving the real CLI against a byte-identical copy of this file with a passing control write (V-1 round 2, WP-5), and the reach was not cosmetic -- mission-dispatch.ps1 passes this file as --settings for EVERY dispatched worker, so R-3's required handoff was unwritable by the role obliged to produce it. The blanket deny is therefore REMOVED so the two exceptions are live, and enforcement of the restriction MOVES TO THE GUARD, which can express deny-a-subtree-except-named-members: see Test-EvidenceWorkerPlanePath in tools/evidence-hooks-next/hooks/lib/evidence-common.ps1, scoped by the runner's LAM_DISPATCH marker and covering the file tools AND the shell. Amendment 15. A template that reads as a restriction while enforcing the opposite is worse than an absent one -- that is this file's own standard, applied to this file.

_memory_off.intent: ADR-032: Claude Code auto memory is disabled in worker and validator sandboxes. Auto memory is persistent agent state OUTSIDE the artifact store, and it can leak implementation history into a later validator -- which is precisely the independence a fresh-identity validator exists to have.
_memory_off.declared_mechanism: spawn with --settings pointing at this file, with the runner-created linked worktree as the process working directory and no --worktree (LAM-ACCEPT amendment 45). REFUTED, AND KEPT HERE SO THE CORRECTION IS READABLE: from 2026-08-30 until LAM-ACCEPT amendment 47 this field declared that the worktree gives the worker a project identity, and therefore an auto-memory directory, different from the orchestrator's; amendment 45 ITEM 1 MEASUREMENT 2 (4) measured otherwise (see separation_obtained). What this file carries is the role's PERMISSION posture; whether a worker spawned this way runs under its defaultMode is NOT isolated (amendment 45 MEASUREMENT 2 (5) read permissionMode default, confounded by the model). This file carries no memory setting and may not carry one (WP-5 K-3 refuses any top-level template key that does not start with an underscore and whose name matches memor).
_memory_off.separation_obtained: NONE AT THE MEMORY-DIRECTORY LAYER, MEASURED: neither the worktree nor this file separates a worker's auto-memory directory. LAM-ACCEPT amendment 45 ITEM 1 MEASUREMENT 2 (4): one probe spawn in a throwaway repository on CLI 2.1.258 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), with the runner's argv, this file handed in via --settings, no --worktree and a pre-placed linked worktree as its working directory reported memory_paths.auto as the MAIN repository's per-project directory, not the tree's; and every recorded init of a real --worktree dispatch that carries the field (lam-smoke session-D-1, -D-1b, -D-1c and -D-2 on 2.1.241, -D-3 on 2.1.252) reported the main repository's project too. From 2026-08-31 until amendment 47 this field read WORKTREE-LEVEL SEPARATION OF THE MEMORY DIRECTORY; no recorded reading ever showed it. It is NOT a proven disable. NOT MEASURED: whether a worker honours the autoMemoryEnabled false recorded in the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json, a file the runner's placement plan includes for every worker tree dispatched from the main checkout (planned read-only, amendment 45 B5 and a validator finding).
_memory_off.disable_status: UNOBTAINABLE ON CLI 2.1.241 (erratum E12). `claude --help` exposes no settings key and no flag that disables auto memory on its own; the only documented control is --bare, which also skips HOOKS, and a worker without hooks has no evidence plane at all. Registered for the operator to close at install time (LAM-INSTALL).

lam_residuals: MEMORY-OFF IS NOT VERIFIED ON THIS CLI BUILD. `claude --help` (2.1.241) exposes no settings key and no flag that disables auto memory on its own; the only documented control is --bare, which also skips HOOKS -- and a worker without hooks has no evidence plane at all, which is a strictly worse failure. Nor does this file separate the memory directory: from 2026-08-30 until LAM-ACCEPT amendment 47 this sentence said the file achieves a worktree-level separation of it, and amendment 45 ITEM 1 MEASUREMENT 2 (4) reads memory_paths.auto under the MAIN repository's project in every recorded init of a --worktree worker dispatch that carries the field (2.1.241, 2.1.252) and in one probe spawn in a throwaway repository without --worktree (2.1.258, this file handed in) -- so what this file achieves is neither a disable nor a separation of the auto-memory directory (see _memory_off.separation_obtained). Stated rather than asserted, per design SS4.5 law 4: a claim with no working detector is an overclaim. Registered for the operator to close at install time (LAM-INSTALL).

The allow entry for .mission/evidence/session-*/ is an ALLOW-SIDE EXEMPTION and carries the residual design SS4.5 law 2 names: it is a standing claim that no other path matches that glob. It exists because the worker's own evidence session lives under the mission plane it is otherwise denied, and it is scoped to the session- prefix rather than to .mission/evidence as a whole.

RULE FORM MATTERS AND THE CLI SAYS SO. An earlier draft of this file wrote each restriction three ways -- Write(path), Edit(path), MultiEdit(path). Claude Code 2.1.241 validates its settings on startup and reported both spellings as defects: 'Write(path) is not matched by file permission checks -- only Edit(path) rules are' and 'MultiEdit(...) matches no known tool'. Edit(path) covers every file-editing tool. The inert spellings are removed rather than left in place, because a rule that reads as a restriction and enforces nothing is worse than an absent one -- a reader budgets for protection that is not there.

These are permission-layer rules, not a boundary. The A1 guard's own doctrine applies unchanged: string inspection of a tool call raises the cost of an accidental write and prevents nothing. Only the worktree and the sandbox make a path unreachable.

EXCEPTION 1 IS STRICTER THAN IT READS, AND THAT IS THE DOCTRINE RATHER THAN A DEFECT. Edit(.mission/evidence/session-*/**) is live at THIS layer, but an agent-side write to it is denied for every role by the protected-path set in the SEALED A1 guard, which this build may not modify -- measured through the real hook on both the file-tool and shell routes. It costs nothing operationally, because a worker's evidence session is written by the HOOKS, harness-side, and never by the worker's tool calls; an agent-writable evidence store would launder testimony as evidence, which is the whole point of that protected set. The allow stays so the closed set reads the same here as in K-3, and this residual is recorded so nobody reads either as a promise that a worker may write there. Amendment 15.
